citations.quote: With the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2N}$, $\rho_N$ is a real-linear isometry. A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum for this scheme is an open set $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^{2N}$ and a supplied continuous map $\beta:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{2N}$.
A solution on an interval $I$ is a function $x:I\to\mathbb R^n$ such that $t_0\in I$, $(t,x(t))\in D$ for every $t\in I$.

The map $F$ is **locally Lipschitz in the state variable, locally uniformly in time**, if every compact time-state cylinder $C\subseteq D$ has a finite $L\ge0$ such that $\|F(t,x)-F(t,y)\|_2\le L\|x-y\|_2$ whenever $(t,x),(t,y)\in C$ have the same time coordinate.

More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make $[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D$, if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

A curve solves the IVP if and only if it satisfies the associated Volterra integral equation. Explicitly, the equation is $x(t)=x_0+\int_{t_0}^{t}F(s,x(s))\,ds$. The integral is oriented, so the assertion applies on either side of $t_0$.

derivations.claim: Choose a compact cylinder inside the open domain, obtain finite field and state-Lipschitz bounds, and select a positive common time radius meeting the quantitative Picard conditions.
Apply the quantitative Picard–Lindelöf result to every initial vector in a smaller coefficient ball, obtaining unique solutions on one common interval in cylinders centered at those vectors.
Use the oriented Volterra form and shared state-Lipschitz constant to bound the trajectory distance by the initial distance plus its time integral, and bound that distance uniformly.
Iterate the integral inequality and bound its final remainder by 4r times (Ld)^m/m!.
Let m tend to infinity to obtain the exponential continuous-dependence estimate, including equality at the base time.
